spans.s:
Kha denotes in the Rigveda and later the hole in the nave of the wheel in which the axle is inserted. There was a difference, it seems, in the size of the hole in the wheel of a cart (anas) and of a chariot (ratha). See also 1. yuga.
Foot notes Rv. viii. 77, 3; 91, 7; x. 156, 3, where only the kha is referred to.
Cf. the adjective su-kha, ‘having a good axle-hole,’ ‘running easily’; later, ‘agreeable.’
Bṛhadāraṇyaka upaniṣad, v. 12, 1 (Mādhyaṃdina; v. 10, 1 kāṇva).
Jaiminīya upaniṣad brāhmaṇa, 1, 3, 6; Geldner, Vedische Studien, 2, 333.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 247.
